loop: Void Drift 0.7.3 release from feat/0-7-0 through protected main and Firebase Hosting, followed by merge-back.
worked: Prepared the 0.7.3 release candidate, recorded the ranked Survival compatibility decision, and kept the fires-in-the-sky challenge unchanged.
Full verification passed after setting the repository's local Java 21 environment; the prepared production bundle passed smoke and hash checks.
Merged the release through protected-main PR #19, published the checked bundle, and passed live checks for hashes, flight, pause, FX Lab, authentication, and score reads without score writes.
Recorded deployment evidence through PR #20 and fast-forwarded feat/0-7-0 to final main for continued work.

issues.observation: I initially treated the mount planner's BREAKING CHANGE footer as a possible app-release version blocker. The user clarified that these JSONs are agent handoff outputs, not a supported import contract.
issues.effect: This introduced an unnecessary compatibility discussion before the release proceeded as 0.7.3.
issues.interpretation: I overread the commit footer without enough product context; the user's clarification resolved the scope.

issues.observation: The first full verification run could not start Firebase emulators because JAVA_HOME and PATH did not point to the installed local Java 21 runtime.
issues.effect: Rules and competition checks did not run in that attempt, so I repeated the full verification with the documented environment; that run passed.
issues.interpretation: The shell environment likely omitted the local toolchain setup; setting JAVA_HOME and PATH fixed the observed failure.

issues.observation: The first release preparation built the site but its smoke test failed to listen on the local preview address with EPERM.
issues.effect: That attempt was retained as failed and preparation had to run again with local preview access; the second bundle passed smoke and release:check.
issues.interpretation: The error indicates the sandbox denied local listener access; the same preparation succeeded when run with that access.

issues.observation: GitHub rejected a direct push to main with GH006 because updates must go through a pull request.
issues.effect: I opened and merged PR #19, then used PR #20 for the post-deployment release record.
issues.interpretation: The protected-branch rule was explicit in the rejection and the PR path completed the release.

issues.observation: I created and pushed v0.7.3 on a local merge commit before the protected-branch PR completed. GitHub produced a different merge commit for main.
issues.effect: The tag temporarily pointed at a non-main merge commit; I force-updated it to the actual PR merge commit before deploying.
issues.interpretation: I assumed the local merge commit would be reused by the protected-main merge. I should have tagged after the PR supplied the final main commit.
